city_vars.market_blurb: Lufkin, Texas serves as a key economic hub for East Texas, historically anchored by the timber and forestry industry due to its location in the Pineywoods region. The city's economy has diversified over time to include manufacturing—particularly oilfield equipment through companies like Lufkin Industries—along with healthcare and retail trade serving surrounding rural counties. As the largest city in Angelina County, Lufkin functions as a regional commercial and medical center.
city_vars.local_note: Lufkin's water supply, drawn largely from groundwater sources, tends to be moderately hard, which can contribute to mineral buildup in water heaters, dishwashers, and washing machines over time. The region experiences frequent severe thunderstorms and occasional tropical storm remnants from the Gulf, leading to periodic power surges and outages that can stress appliance electronics and compressors.
city_vars.city_spotlight:
Lufkin sits at the heart of the Piney Woods, serving as the commercial anchor for Deep East Texas and the seat of Angelina County. The surrounding forests built the city's original economy, and timber and wood products manufacturing still run deep in its identity, though the modern base has broadened considerably. Lufkin Industries' oil field equipment work, alongside healthcare, education, retail, and government offices, now gives the local economy a sturdier, more diverse footing than its lumber-town roots alone.

With roughly 34,000 residents, Lufkin feels sized just right — big enough for full-service hospitals, a community college, and steady employers, yet small enough that neighborhoods like Crown Colony and Kurth still carry a distinct, close-knit character. It's a working city, proud of its piney landscape and its role as the region's steady hub.

columns.heading: Won't Drain
columns.text: Dishwasher not draining can result from clogs in the drain hose, filter blockages, or a faulty drain pump. Our technicians diagnose the cause and clear or replace the affected component to restore proper drainage.

columns.heading: Leaking Water
columns.text: A dishwasher leaking water may indicate a worn door seal, cracked tub, or loose inlet valve. Wells Appliance Repair's technicians locate the source and repair or replace seals and valves to stop leaks.

columns.heading: Not Cleaning Dishes
columns.text: Poor cleaning performance often stems from clogged spray arms, worn wash impellers, or a malfunctioning motor. Our technicians inspect and repair these components so your dishes come out spotless every time.

columns.heading: Won't Start
columns.text: A dishwasher that won't start may have a faulty door latch, defective control board, or blown thermal fuse. Wells Appliance Repair's technicians test and replace the failed part to restore normal operation.

columns.heading: Not Heating Water
columns.text: If your dishwasher isn't heating water, the heating element or thermostat may be broken. Our technicians test these components and install replacements to ensure hot water cycles work properly.

columns.heading: Loud or Vibrating
columns.text: Excessive noise or vibration often comes from worn pump bearings, loose spray arms, or foreign objects in the tub. Wells Appliance Repair diagnoses the source and repairs or replaces worn parts for quiet operation.

fq_items.question: What should I do if my Whirlpool dishwasher won't drain?
fq_items.answer: A Whirlpool dishwasher that won't drain usually indicates a clogged filter, blocked drain hose, or pump malfunction. First, check the filter basket for food debris and rinse it thoroughly. If that doesn't help, the drain hose may be kinked or obstructed, or the drain pump itself may need replacement. These issues require professional diagnosis to avoid further damage. Contact Wells Appliance Repair for a prompt inspection.

fq_items.question: Why is my Whirlpool dishwasher leaking under the sink?
fq_items.answer: Leaks typically stem from a cracked or misaligned door seal, failed tub gasket, loose inlet hose connection, or internal pump damage. Some leaks develop slowly and only appear during the wash cycle. Never ignore pooling water—it can damage cabinetry and create mold. Our technicians will locate the source and repair or replace the faulty component to restore your dishwasher's watertight seal.

fq_items.question: Should I repair my Whirlpool dishwasher or buy a new one?
fq_items.answer: Repair is often the smart choice if your dishwasher is under 8–10 years old and the repair cost is reasonable. Wells Appliance Repair will provide an honest assessment so you can decide. We'll explain what's wrong, what the fix entails, and whether replacement makes sense for your situation. Most component failures in mid-life units are economical to repair versus the expense and hassle of a full replacement.

fq_items.question: What causes a Whirlpool dishwasher to stop cleaning dishes properly?
fq_items.answer: Poor cleaning often results from a clogged spray arm, worn pump impeller, low water pressure, faulty heating element, or detergent dispenser malfunction. Hard water deposits can also block the spray nozzles. The issue may also stem from overloading or incorrect cycle selection, but if you've ruled those out, professional service is needed. We'll diagnose the root cause and restore your dishwasher's cleaning power.

fq_items.question: How can I prevent my Whirlpool dishwasher from leaking again?
fq_items.answer: After repair, rinse dishes thoroughly to prevent buildup in the filter and spray arms, which can strain the pump. Run the empty dishwasher monthly to keep seals pliable. Avoid overloading, which stresses door seals. Inspect hose connections annually for cracks or looseness. If you notice small leaks reappearing, contact us right away—early intervention prevents major water damage to your kitchen.
